newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $74 mln trade gap July 1-13.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $74 mln trade gap July 1-13.

text.p: Brazil posted a trade gap of $74 million between July 1-13, with exports of $2.085 billion and imports of $2.159 billion, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said.
The ministry said in a statement that the country saw a $50 million trade surplus in the second week of the month, with exports of $1.164 billion and imports of $1.114 billion.
The surplus in the second week reduced a trade deficit that was running at $124 million at the end of July's first week.
The ministry said average daily exports so far this month were at $231.7 million while average daily imports were $239.9 million.
In the second week of the month, average daily exports of $232.8 million exceeded average daily imports of $222.8 million.
In June, the country posted a $466 million trade gap, taking the deficit for the first half of the year to over $4.7 billion against $5.5 billion for the whole of 1996.
